tool_input.command:
mkdir -p forgemyspec-bundle/expense-splitter && cat > forgemyspec-board.yaml <<'EOF'
requirements:
  - id: R1
    status: doing
    title: "CLI expense splitter"
    quote: "Build a CLI expense splitter in Python. Record expenses for a group (payer, amount, description, participants; split equally among participants), persist them in a JSON file, show each person's balance, and compute a settlement plan with the minimum number of transfers using a greedy algorithm. Single file expense_splitter.py, stdlib only."
    steps:
      - {do: "Write and lint spec.yaml", check: "cmd: PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/expense-splitter/spec.yaml --formal"}
      - {do: "User approves the spec bundle", ok: false}
      - {do: "Implement expense_splitter.py and tests, gate passes", ok: false}
    next: "lint, package, then request approval"
EOF
cat > forgemyspec-bundle/expense-splitter/spec.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "0.1"
title: CLI expense splitter
objective: >-
  A single-file, stdlib-only Python CLI (expense_splitter.py) that records group expenses split equally among
  participants, persists them in a JSON file, shows each person's balance and computes a greedy settlement plan.
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Python 3 stdlib only; single module expense_splitter.py at the repository root; tests with unittest in tests/."
  assumptions:
    - "Amounts are decimal with at most 2 places and are stored as integer cents to avoid float error."
    - "When an amount does not divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first participants in sorted name order, so shares always sum exactly to the amount."
    - "The payer need not be a participant; a payer outside the participants is credited the full amount and owes nothing."
    - "Greedy (largest creditor pays by largest debtor) gives at most n-1 transfers; it is not guaranteed to be the true minimum, which is NP-hard in general."
    - "Names are case-sensitive, non-empty strings; the default data file is expenses.json in the current directory, overridable with --file."
constraints:
  - "Single file expense_splitter.py; standard library only, no third-party packages."
  - "No floating-point money arithmetic."
  - "No unequal or percentage splits, currencies, expense editing or deletion, or network access."
success_criteria:
  - "add, list, balances and settle subcommands work end to end against a JSON file."
  - "Applying the settlement plan brings every balance to zero."
  - "All boundary tests pass under the gate."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "Adding an expense records payer, amount, description and participants, split equally with shares summing exactly to the amount.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Expenses persist in a JSON file and are reloaded by later invocations; a missing file is an empty ledger.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h3, description: "The balances command shows each person's net balance (paid minus share), and balances sum to zero.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h4, description: "The settle command outputs a greedy plan of at most n-1 transfers that zeroes every balance.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h5, description: "Invalid input (bad amount, empty participants, corrupt JSON) exits with status 2 and a message, without changing the file.", confidence: 0.85}
required_evidence:
  - "Output of the unittest run for tests/ with all tests passing."
  - "Gate report ending in RESULT: PASS."
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Implement ledger, equal split and JSON persistence in expense_splitter.py", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Implement balances and the greedy settlement plan", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h3, h4]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Implement argparse CLI with input validation and exit codes", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h5]}
  - {id: a4, description: "Run unittest boundary tests and the gate", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
decision_rules:
  - "If a requirement needs unequal splits or currencies, stop and amend the spec."
  - "If a test fails, fix the code, never the test, unless the spec is wrong; then amend."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a CLI expense splitter in Python. Record expenses for a group (payer, amount, description, participants; split equally among participants), persist them in a JSON file, show each person's balance, and compute a settlement plan with the minimum number of transfers using a greedy algorithm. Single file expense_splitter.py, stdlib only."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "equal split among participants"
      - "persisted in JSON file"
      - "balance per person"
      - "greedy settlement plan"
      - "single file expense_splitter.py"
      - "stdlib only"
formal:
  module: ExpenseSplitter
  obligations:
    - id: equal_split_exact
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Shares of an expense are equal up to one cent, sum exactly to the amount in cents, and leftover cents go to the first participants in sorted order."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["equal split among participants"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.SplitTests.test_shares_sum_exactly"
    - id: json_persistence
      kind: boundary
      statement: "An added expense is written to the JSON file and reloaded by a fresh load; a missing file loads as an empty ledger."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["persisted in JSON file"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.PersistenceTests.test_roundtrip_and_missing_file"
    - id: balances_per_person
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Balance of each person is paid minus share; the balances sum to zero."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["balance per person"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.BalanceTests.test_balances_sum_to_zero"
    - id: greedy_plan_settles
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The plan pairs the largest debtor with the largest creditor, has at most n-1 transfers, and applying it zeroes all balances."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["greedy settlement plan"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.SettleTests.test_plan_zeroes_balances"
    - id: invalid_input_exit_2
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Invalid amount, empty participants or corrupt JSON exits 2 with a message and leaves the file unchanged."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["persisted in JSON file"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.CliTests.test_invalid_input_exits_2"
    - id: single_file_stdlib
      kind: boundary
      statement: "expense_splitter.py imports only standard library modules and is the only module the tests import from the project."
      hypotheses: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]
      must_include: ["single file expense_splitter.py", "stdlib only"]
      test: "test_expense_splitter.StructureTests.test_stdlib_only_imports"
scope:
  paths: ["expense_splitter.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
export PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness
python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/expense-splitter/spec.yaml --formal && python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/expense-splitter/spec.yaml; python3 -m forgemyspec board

result:
The spec is written and lints clean at 100/100, and the bundle is packaged. Nothing is built yet, because the spec needs your approval first.

**Obligations** (all `boundary`, so this is a spec-only bundle with no Dafny proofs):

| id | statement |
|---|---|
| `equal_split_exact` | Shares are equal up to one cent and sum exactly to the amount. Leftover cents go to the first participants in sorted order. |
| `json_persistence` | An added expense is written to the JSON file and reloaded. A missing file loads as an empty ledger. |
| `balances_per_person` | Each person's balance is paid minus share, and the balances sum to zero. |
| `greedy_plan_settles` | The largest debtor pays the largest creditor, with at most n-1 transfers. Applying the plan zeroes every balance. |
| `invalid_input_exit_2` | A bad amount, empty participants or corrupt JSON exits with status 2 and a message, and the file keeps its previous content. |
| `single_file_stdlib` | `expense_splitter.py` imports only standard library modules. |

**Assumptions you're approving:**
- Amounts are stored as integer cents, so there is no float arithmetic.
- Leftover cents from an uneven split go one each to the first participants in sorted name order.
- The payer doesn't have to be one of the participants.
- The default data file is `expenses.json`. You can override it with `--file`.
- Greedy gives at most n-1 transfers but is not guaranteed to be the true minimum, which is NP-hard in general. You asked for the minimum using a greedy algorithm, so I'm reading that as "greedy, which is the best this approach can do". Tell me if you want an exact minimum instead.

To approve, type the code **ICHCT2** in the chat. Then I'll run `approve` and implement `expense_splitter.py` with its tests.

I couldn't add the requirement to `forgemyspec-board.yaml` because the guard blocks that file until a spec covers it. I'll add it after approval.
